literature_hypothesis.title: A neural circuit for olfactory motion detection
literature_hypothesis.scope: Female-fly physiology and FlyWire/connectomic evidence motivate il3LN6 and DA1 ALPN as candidate olfactory-motion circuit roles. They do not establish MaleCNS body identity or prove the same computation in MaleCNS.

connectivity_contract.selection: Only edges for annotation-resolved candidate body IDs may enter the audit.
connectivity_contract.interpretation: Structural synapse weight only. No dynamical sign, delay, or functional motion computation is inferred from an edge.

allowed: MaleCNS v1.0 contains annotation-matched candidate cells of the reported types, if found.
Exact candidate-to-candidate MaleCNS structural edges and aggregate weights may be reported from the frozen weight table.
Cross-dataset literature may motivate a candidate role when explicitly labeled indirect.
forbidden: MaleCNS il3LN6 computes odor motion without MaleCNS-specific functional evidence.
A FlyWire, hemibrain, or VFB body ID is automatically the same body ID in MaleCNS v1.0.
Structural connectivity establishes a 40 ms inhibitory delay.
This audit supports navigation or source-finding performance claims.

stop_rules: Do not hand-add a body ID because it appears in another connectome.
Do not broaden a regex after seeing navigation performance.
If il3LN6 or DA1_lPN do not resolve from v1.0 annotations, report a blocked audit rather than substitute a neighboring type.
If DA1_ORN naming does not resolve cleanly, keep the motif incomplete and audit ORN identity separately.
